summary_en: This study tests SOT109, an antibody aimed at CDH17 linked to a payload called exatecan, in people with advanced, unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer. SOT109 is given into a vein (IV) over about 30 minutes (±15 minutes) once every 21 days. The study has two parts, and the record does not state a primary outcome; it is a Phase 1/2 study of safety, pharmacokinetics and preliminary efficacy, with Part A looking at safety and dose levels and Part B comparing two safe dose levels for benefit and risk.
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa SOT109, un anticuerpo dirigido a CDH17 unido a una carga llamada exatecán, en personas con cáncer colorrectal avanzado, no resecable o metastásico. SOT109 se administra por vena (IV) durante unos 30 minutos (±15 minutos), una vez cada 21 días. El estudio tiene dos partes, y el registro no indica una medida de resultado principal; es un estudio de fase 1/2 de seguridad, farmacocinética y eficacia preliminar, en el que la Parte A evalúa la seguridad y las dosis, y la Parte B compara dos dosis seguras para determinar el equilibrio entre beneficio y riesgo.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who can give written informed consent.
Advanced unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer, confirmed by tissue or cell testing.
ECOG performance score 0-1; score of 2 to be discussed with the sponsor.
Progressed on fluoropyrimidines, oxaliplatin, irinotecan and bevacizumab, with no further standard treatment options.
Blood counts, kidney, liver, heart and other lab values within the protocol limits.
not_for: Radiation therapy within 14 days before the first dose, or unrecovered side effects from it.
Systemic therapy for metastatic cancer other than colorectal cancer, apart from listed exceptions.
History of interstitial pneumonitis or pulmonary fibrosis.
Symptomatic central nervous system tumors, or peripheral sensory neuropathy grade 2 or higher.
Recent serious heart events, or a history of inflammatory bowel disease.
